title: Nanofiltration System

introduction.definition: A nanofiltration system forces water at moderate pressure through spiral-wound membrane elements. NF lets water and most monovalent salts through but rejects hardness (calcium, magnesium), sulphate, colour and many organic molecules. Elements are housed in pressure vessels arranged in stages to increase recovery.

pressure.title: Feed pressure overcomes osmotic pressure
pressure.description: Nanofiltration needs a feed pressure of roughly 5–20 bar (between UF and reverse osmosis). Water and most monovalent ions pass; divalent ions (hardness, sulphate) and organics above ~ 200–1000 Da are largely rejected. Pressure falls slightly along each vessel; stage 2 treats the stage 1 concentrate to raise recovery.

video_tutorials.title: Nanofiltration System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Nanofiltration System.
A nanofiltration system forces water at moderate pressure through spiral-wound membrane elements.
NF lets water and most monovalent salts through but rejects hardness (calcium, magnesium), sulphate, colour and many organic molecules.
Elements are housed in pressure vessels arranged in stages to increase recovery.
Typical applications include water softening and colour removal; sulphate removal from seawater (oil-field injection); food and dairy (demineralisation); wastewater reuse.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: FRP Pressure Vessels (stage 1: two, stage 2: one), High-Pressure Feed Pump (multistage), High-Pressure Feed Pump (multistage) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Nanofiltration System — Operation

script.narration: How the Nanofiltration System works.
The cartridge pre-filter protects the elements.
The high-pressure pump raises the feed pressure.
Feed flows along the element spacers; water permeates the membrane leaves.
Stage-1 concentrate feeds stage 2.
Permeate and concentrate leave through their headers.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Nanofiltration needs a feed pressure of roughly 5–20 bar (between UF and reverse osmosis).

video_tutorials.title: Nanofiltration System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Nanofiltration System.
Record pressures, flows, conductivity; normalise data.
CIP when normalised flow drops ~ 10–15 %.
Replace elements (typically 3–7 years).
Watch for scaling: rising δp in last stage, falling flow. Common cause: exceeding solubility (caso₄, caco₃).
Watch for fouling: first-stage δp rise. Common cause: colloids, biofilm.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
